name: RV Checklist
description: A complete overview for RV owners covering systems, supplies, safety and pre-trip basics for motorhomes and towable trailers.

items.text: Fresh water tank, pump and city water connection
Gray and black water tanks and dump valves
12V battery system and shore-power hookup
Propane system for furnace, stove and fridge
Slide-outs, leveling and stabilizer jacks
Chassis, tires and braking system
Leveling blocks and wheel chocks
Drinking-water-safe fresh hose and a sewer hose kit
Electrical adapter and surge protector
Disposable gloves and tank treatment chemicals
Basic toolkit, duct tape and spare fuses
Kitchen basics, bedding and camp chairs
Test smoke, carbon monoxide and propane detectors
items.note: Replace batteries and check expiry dates

items.text: Keep fire extinguishers charged and accessible
Stock a well-supplied first aid kit
Carry road safety triangles or flares
Know your RV's height, length and weight limits
Carry a tire pressure gauge and basic emergency kit
Check tire pressure and inspect for wear or damage
Confirm fluids, brakes and engine are road-ready
Secure all interior items and close cabinets
Retract slides, steps, antenna and awning
Disconnect or secure water, power and waste hookups
Do a full walk-around and test running lights
Level the RV and place wheel chocks
Connect to shore power through a surge protector
Hook up fresh water and waste as needed
Extend slide-outs and stabilizer jacks
Turn on propane appliances and confirm they work
Inspect roof seals and seams for leaks
Service the chassis, brakes and wheel bearings
Sanitize the fresh water system periodically
Check and clean the air conditioner and furnace
Test batteries and keep them charged in storage

faq.q: What systems should every RV owner understand?
faq.a: Learn the fresh, gray and black water systems, the 12V and shore-power electrical systems, the propane system for heat, cooking and the fridge, and the chassis and tires. Knowing how each works makes setup, troubleshooting and maintenance far easier.

faq.q: What supplies should I always keep in the RV?
faq.a: Keep leveling blocks, wheel chocks, a fresh-water hose, a sewer hose and gloves, an electrical adapter and surge protector, basic tools, and kitchen and bedding basics. A stocked RV means less to forget and a faster setup at each stop.

faq.q: What safety gear does an RV need?
faq.a: Maintain working smoke, carbon monoxide and propane detectors, fire extinguishers, and a first aid kit. Carry a tire pressure gauge, road safety triangles and know your RV's height and weight to avoid low bridges and overloading.

faq.q: What are the basic pre-trip checks?
faq.a: Check tire pressure and condition, confirm everything inside is secured, retract slides and steps, disconnect or secure hookups, do a full walk-around, and verify lights and brakes before pulling out. These basics prevent the most common departure mistakes.

faq.q: Can I print this RV checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it in the RV and tick off systems, supplies, safety and pre-trip basics whenever you need a quick reference.
